newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanians seize ship, head for Italy.
newsitem.headline: Albanians seize ship, head for Italy.

text.p: A merchant ship with scores of Albanians on board was heading for the southern Italian port of Brindisi under an Italian navy escort on Thursday, coastguards said.

The Italian news agency ANSA named the ship as the Saint Vincent-registered "Giorgios" and said Albanians fleeing unrest in their country had stormed aboard it in the port of Durres and forced it to set sail.
The agency, also quoting coastguards, said there might be as many as 400 Albanians on board.

A coastguard spokesman in the southern port of Bari contacted by telephone by Reuters confirmed the ship was heading for Italy but had no details about the vessel. He said 100 to 150 people could be on board.
"It is heading for Brindisi with a navy escort," the spokesman said.
ANSA said the port of Durres was not officially closed but all ships had moved away from the harbour.

The ferry "Annemaria Lauro", which links the southern Italian port of Otranto to Durres, was moored off the harbour after a crowd of Albanians tried to storm it while other Italian ferries left Albania early or turned back to Italy, it said.
The situation in Albania slid closer to anarchy on Thursday as arms depots in several towns including the capital Tirana were looted and food warehouses were raided.
Rebels have seized control of the south in an anti-government uprising sparked by anger over the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.
